sources.publisher: Jasper Verschuur (repository owner; dataset authorship requires review)
described_content: event and port identifiers with country, name, year and date
reported reduction, shutdown and recovery durations
vessel-activity time series for affected and unaffected ports
known_limitations: a repository presence does not establish redistribution rights
a public repository does not by itself grant a data licence
vessel activity is a proxy and must not be relabelled as cargo throughput or delivered service
operational definitions, time resolution, completeness and source provenance require inspection before scoring

sources.publisher: Chenchen Kuai and collaborators (dataset repository: ChenchenMobility)
described_content: daily vessel counts at principal U.S. ports for 2015 through 2023
1927 port-cyclone interaction records with exposure and port response metadata
meteorological and tide variables including storm-surge-related measurements
port characteristics and published resilience/network metrics
known_limitations: the overall README declares CC BY 4.0 but each included source component and any third-party material must be checked for separate terms and attribution requirements
the published scope focuses on U.S. principal ports and tropical cyclones, so it does not establish general validity for strikes, cyber incidents, equipment failures or global ports
port-cyclone interaction rows are not independent events; group all related ports, windows and derived records by cyclone episode before train/calibration/test splitting
published resilience metrics may be derived from the same base observations; recompute target metrics independently and do not treat derived columns as independent ground truth
inspect exact temporal granularity, field definitions, missingness, source lineage, revision policy and event-window selection before use
catalog metadata describes summary throughput metrics, not necessarily incident-level time series
temporal granularity and port coverage must be inspected from the actual resource before use
do not infer the onset, recovery, causal mechanism or counterfactual effect of a disruption from aggregate summary metrics alone
pin exact retrieved metadata and data bytes because an API view identifier does not freeze its contents

corpus_design.leakage_policy: All ports, time points, revised reports and derived labels tied to one event remain in one split. Do not train on observations or reports published after the historical decision time being evaluated.
corpus_design.holdout_policy: Freeze a temporal holdout before fitting or tuning. Use leave-one-port-out only when the independent port count and data support it.
forbidden_inferences: no observed recovery equals zero recovery time
summary throughput alone proves a disruption cause
synthetic test success proves historical predictive validity

episode_record_contract.time_semantics: Distinguish event time, publication/issue time, retrieval time, and the earliest time the decision process could have known each fact.
episode_record_contract.censoring_semantics: If recovery is not observed before the source window ends, record right_censored or unknown; never encode it as a recovery time of zero.
episode_record_contract.counterfactual_semantics: An unaffected port is a candidate control, not automatically a valid counterfactual. Document matching variables, shared shocks, spillovers and exclusions.

capture_gates: A source must be pinned or captured with exact bytes before it can enter a scored corpus.
Rights, attribution and source-use restrictions must be resolved before redistributing source bytes or derived products where restrictions apply.
Every episode label must trace to source rows and a documented operational definition.
All observations for one episode are grouped before any train/calibration/test split.
All transformations preserve an input-to-output digest lineage and a reproducible command/configuration.
A source discovery record is never counted as a captured artifact or a validated observation.
No historical predictive claim is admitted until the baseline and held-out evaluation protocol are frozen.
